cost_policy: PP-OCRv6 Medium is roughly forty times slower per case than Tiny, so a configuration reaches Medium only after cheaper engines show it is worth measuring.

stages.name: stored-evidence analysis without OCR rerun
stages.description: Read the merged v1 report, the frozen protocol, the corpus manifest and the production worker OCR path. Established that the merged report stores per-case metrics but no OCR blocks, so failure decomposition requires a block-level capture; and that the production worker performs no downscaling at all, so the benchmark's 960-pixel long-edge bound is a benchmark-only preprocessing choice.
stages.promotion: A block-level capture harness is required before any taxonomy can be evidence-backed.

stages.name: cheap-engine capture and resolution sensitivity
stages.description: Captured every exposed development case for the two cheapest engines across the bounded resolution matrix. Verified each baseline capture reproduces the merged per-case measurement exactly before trusting any derived number.
stages.promotion: Resolution changed exact-title recovery by at most one case in either direction for both engines, so no resolution above the baseline was promoted on title-quality grounds. Higher raster settings did materially reduce whole-page WER, so dpi180-edge1920 was promoted for the WER decomposition only.

stages.name: mid-size confirmation
stages.description: Confirmed on a second neural engine that the Tiny resolution result was not engine-specific.
stages.promotion: Small reproduced the Tiny pattern (+1 exact title, materially lower WER at higher raster). No further resolution configuration was promoted to Medium.

stages.name: Medium at the baseline configuration only
stages.description: Medium was measured across the full exposed corpus at the merged baseline configuration so its failure decomposition is directly comparable with the merged evidence.
stages.promotion: No higher-resolution Medium run was justified: Tiny and Small showed no material title-quality gain from resolution, and Medium already exceeds every operational ceiling at the baseline configuration, so a slower configuration could not become a candidate.

stages.name: controlled full-poster title stroke A/B probe
stages.description: Single-variable A/B probe over complete posters. The stroke variant is proved pixel-identical to the corpus asset for all 48 cases before OCR runs, and title position is held fixed, so the two variants differ only by the one-pixel title glyph dilation. Layout, section headings, body text, noise, contrast and the decorative title shadow are all present. Both the merged production selector and the best development selector are scored.
stages.promotion: Terminal stage. It measures how sensitive the tested PP-OCRv6 candidates are to one corpus rendering choice, and reports the union of exact recoveries across that tested candidate set. It does not establish a theoretical or model-independent ceiling: an unseen model, a different recognition architecture or another legitimate deterministic configuration could behave differently.
